[h1] Story [/h1] Wir spielen einen Ritter (oder Magier) der aus dem Königreich verbannt wurde und nur zurückkehren kann, wenn er den Heiligen Grahl findet 

[h1] Gameplay [/h1] Genau wie auch das andere Spiel von diesem Entwickler (Shotgun Legend), erinnert es sehr stark an Legend of Zelda vom NES. Im Gegensatz zu Shotgun Legend, ist hier der Gameplay Fokus eher auf Roguelike ausgelegt. Wir starten im Dungeon wo die einzelnen Maps Random erstellt werden, nach 5 Maps kommt ein Raum wo wir Leben oder Waffen für Gold kaufen können & danach kommt ein Boss Kampf. Die Boss Kämpfe sind wieder sehr gut gelungen. In den einzelnen Leveln, weichen wir verschiedene Feinde aus & sammeln dabei Waffen & Gold ein. Natürlich können wir mit unseren Waffen auch Feinde besiegen aber Waffen sind nicht unendlich einsetzbar sondern es gibt 4 Slots für die 4 verschiedenen Waffen. Der Ritter ist im vergleich zu dem Magier fast Nutzlos und erschwert einem das Spiel. Der Magier kann sich nämlich selber heilen was das ganze einfacher macht

[h1] Achievement Schwierigkeit 4/10 [/h1] Es gibt insgesamt 22 Erfolge. Hierfür muss man das Spiel beenden, von jedem Waffen oder Zauber Typ 5 gleichzeitig halten, bis zu 1000 Gold im Inventar haben, 50.000 Punkte erzielen & 25 mal sterben. Das wohl schwerste ist hier die 50K Punkte zu erreichen & die 1K Gold im Inventar zu haben ohne davon etwas auszugeben. Broken Armor is a top-down 2D action game developed by Jonathan Tindell and published by Wastebasket Games that deliberately embraces the spirit of early arcade and home-computer titles. Rather than attempting to modernize its structure with sprawling systems or cinematic storytelling, it commits fully to a retro philosophy centered on challenge, repetition, and mechanical simplicity. The premise follows a disgraced knight cast out from his homeland and sent on a quest to retrieve a sacred relic in hopes of reclaiming his honor. The narrative functions primarily as a framing device, giving players a reason to descend into dangerous halls filled with monsters and hazards, but the real emphasis lies in moment-to-moment survival and score-driven progression.

From a visual standpoint, Broken Armor wears its nostalgia proudly. The pixel-art style intentionally mirrors the limitations of older systems, evoking the look and feel of early computer and arcade games. The environments are composed of compact rooms connected in dungeon-like sequences, each populated with enemies, traps, and environmental obstacles. The aesthetic is simple, yet cohesive, reinforcing the game’s old-school identity. This stripped-down presentation may not appeal to players seeking elaborate visuals, but it complements the gameplay’s focus on clarity and responsiveness. Every sprite, projectile, and hazard is easily readable, which becomes essential during intense encounters.

Gameplay revolves around navigating procedurally assembled floors while battling waves of enemies that range from basic creatures to more dangerous foes with unique attack patterns. The top-down perspective encourages careful positioning and constant movement, as enemies often swarm from multiple directions. Combat mechanics are straightforward, typically involving ranged attacks and dodging rather than complex combo systems. However, the simplicity does not equate to ease. The game is deliberately unforgiving, and careless mistakes can quickly result in defeat. This emphasis on challenge creates a loop of learning and mastery, where each failed attempt provides insight into enemy behavior and optimal positioning strategies.

Resource management adds another layer of tension. Weapons and items are limited, and players must decide when to engage aggressively and when to conserve supplies. Environmental hazards such as pools that slow movement or inflict damage increase the stakes of each encounter, forcing players to remain aware of their surroundings. Boss battles punctuate progression through the dungeon floors, presenting larger threats with distinct patterns that require observation and patience to overcome. These encounters serve as skill checks, rewarding players who have internalized the game’s core mechanics.

Replayability is a central pillar of Broken Armor’s design. Because the dungeon layouts and enemy placements are randomized, each run feels slightly different. The inclusion of leaderboards and achievements encourages competitive play and personal improvement. Additionally, the availability of alternative playable characters, such as a mage introduced through additional content, expands strategic possibilities. Each character offers subtle variations in combat style, giving players incentive to experiment and refine different approaches to the game’s challenges.

Community reception reflects the game’s niche appeal. Many players appreciate its dedication to old-school design principles, praising its difficulty curve and the satisfaction that comes from gradual mastery. Fans of retro-inspired titles often find its simplicity refreshing in an era dominated by sprawling, system-heavy releases. On the other hand, some players view its mechanics as overly basic and its presentation as too minimalistic by modern standards. For those accustomed to highly polished and feature-rich indie titles, Broken Armor may feel austere or limited.

Ultimately, Broken Armor succeeds on its own terms. It does not attempt to reinvent the action genre or compete with larger productions. Instead, it delivers a focused, challenging experience that captures the essence of early arcade design. Its blend of procedural dungeons, tight combat, and high difficulty creates a loop that rewards persistence and skill development. For players who appreciate retro aesthetics and uncompromising challenge, Broken Armor offers a concise yet engaging adventure that proves simplicity, when paired with thoughtful design, can remain compelling long after the era it draws inspiration from has passed.

Broken Armor is a tiny retro platformer where you play as a knight who has, quite literally, lost his drip. Your armor is gone, your dignity is questionable, and you’re running around a trap-filled dungeon in what is basically medieval underwear trying not to get turned into red pixels.

You’re not the Chosen One.
You’re the **Dropped One**. As in: dropped your helmet, dropped your shield, dropped into a pit.

---

### Pros

* Simple, clear premise:

  * Step 1: Escape dungeon
  * Step 2: Don’t touch anything sharp
  * Step 3: That’s it, there is no step 3
* One-hit deaths and tight levels make every jump feel like an exam you did *not* revise for.
* Charming retro visuals: it looks like the kind of game that would have ruined your childhood on a floppy disk.
* Instant respawns, so your failure montage is seamless and efficient.
* Great “just one more attempt” energy that turns into “why is it 2 a.m. and why am I still shirtless and impaled.”

---

### Cons

* No armor means everything is lethal:

  * Spikes? Dead.
  * Arrows? Dead.
  * Looking at an enemy funny? Emotionally dead.
* Some jumps are very “pixel perfect,” and by pixel perfect I mean “you will swear the game is lying.”
* The story is basically “you lost your armor, good luck,” which is relatable but not exactly deep lore.
* You will start blaming the controls, the level design, the keyboard, gravity, your chair… anything except your thumbs.

---

### Peak Broken Armor Moments

* Landing a crazy series of jumps flawlessly, then walking face-first into a stationary spike at the finish line.
* Taking a break because you’re tilted, coming back, beating a level first try and pretending that was always the plan.
* Standing at the edge of a gap for 30 seconds debating your entire existence before missing the jump by one pixel.
* Realizing that if your knight had just worn a second layer that morning, this entire game wouldn’t exist.

---

这款游戏是一款由 Jonathan Tindell 开发、Wastebasket Games 发行的像素风格动作游戏，于 2016 年 8 月 1 日发布，支持 Windows 平台。

⚔️ 核心玩法：复古风格的动作挑战

✅ 优点：
复古的游戏氛围：采用类似 5.25 英寸软盘时代的像素图形，营造出浓厚的怀旧感。 

高重玩性：程序生成的关卡和敌人配置，使每次游玩都充满新鲜感。 

挑战性的成就系统：设有如“50K 分数”等高难度成就，适合追求极限挑战的玩家。 

❌ 缺点：
操作手感一般：部分玩家反映游戏的操作不够流畅，可能影响体验。

内容重复性高：尽管关卡是随机生成的，但敌人种类和机制较为有限，可能导致游戏后期体验重复。

存在 BUG：部分玩家报告在特定情况下会遇到无法继续游戏的 BUG。

🎯 总结：
《Broken Armor》是一款融合了复古风格与现代 Roguelite 元素的动作游戏，适合喜欢挑战和怀旧风格的玩家。尽管存在一些不足，但其独特的游戏机制和丰富的内容仍值得一试。

"A Hidden Gem for Retro Platformer Fans!"
Broken Armor is a small but mighty game that feels like a love letter to the challenging platformers of the past. While it might not be on everyone’s radar in 2024, it’s proof that minimalist design and tight gameplay can still deliver a ton of fun for those willing to give it a shot.

Gameplay:
You play as a fragile knight whose armor breaks right at the start, leaving you vulnerable to every threat. The game’s charm lies in its simplicity—jump, dodge, and survive. The controls are tight, and the levels are designed to test your precision and patience. Each stage is packed with hazards, and the satisfaction of clearing a tough section is unmatched. It’s tough, but it never feels unfair.

Graphics and Sound:
The pixel-art visuals are simple yet effective, giving off a classic retro vibe. The music and sound effects fit perfectly, immersing you in the game’s nostalgic feel. It’s not about flashy graphics—it’s about creating a focused and engaging experience.

Pros:

Tight and responsive controls.
Challenging but rewarding gameplay.
Retro aesthetic that captures the essence of old-school platformers.
Perfect for quick play sessions.
Cons:

The difficulty might deter casual players.
Very short; could leave you wanting more.
Conclusion:
Broken Armor isn’t trying to compete with modern AAA titles—it’s a game for players who appreciate the simplicity and challenge of classic platformers. While most gamers today might overlook it, those who enjoy tough, retro-style games will find it a hidden gem. It’s a short but satisfying journey that reminded me why I love indie games in the first place.

Ignoring the money making bug, this game is incredible. Very addicting and difficult. Found myself sitting down for 3 hours playing this game.

O jogo é um zelda porém mais quebrado. A mecanica do jogo gira em torno de vc acumular recursos para usá-los da maneira mais sábia possível. Ele não é tão difícil quanto parece ser, e como os próprios desenvolvedores pintam nas conquistas, terminei ele na minha segunda run jogando de mago.

Broken Armor es uno de esos juegos que intentan recuperar la esencia de los juegos de antaño, pero a diferencia de los otros, este juego sí que lo hace y no abusa de sonidos retro ni de referencias a otros juegos antiguos.

Su tipografía, jugabilidad, logros, sonidos, sistema de puntuación, etc... Es lo que le da la esencia añeja a este juego. Realmente he disfrutado jugarlo ya que es bastante adictivo y te hace seguirlo jugando tras cada muerta. Al principio el juego puede resultar difícil o injusto pero a la larga que vas jugando más fácil se hace y más disfrutable.

P.S: Borren y mutilen a los malditos slimes venenosos, murciélagos rojos, serpientes y el jefe de la banda de murciélagos, URGENTE. El mago >>>>> El caballero.

Игра хороша, не из самых легких, мне понравилась. Поиграл на клавиатуре и геймпаде, второй вариант удобнее. 
Один раз дошел до черного рыцаря и проиграл. Потом когда я второй раз до него дошел, я убил его, подумал конец, но я ошибался. Но понял я это когда умер после черного рыцаря, после него очередная комната, я умер от красных летучих мышей и не успел ничего понять. Теперь нужно пройти заново. Удобнее играть не геймпаде, если он у вас есть, играйте с ним. 
UPD: После рыцаря идёт комната по которой надо дойти до конца и взять кубок. Но эта комната длинная. Затем игра начинается заново для получения больших очков (для достижений).
P.S. Решил вот на все достижения пройти. Достижение на 50к очков - проверка на стойкость, ты можешь набрать 49к а потом тебя может убить каракатица или летучая мышь.
UPD: Я проигрывал на высоких рекордах. И на 39к, и на 43к, и на 46к, но всё же прошел. В общем игру могу советовать.
